messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Dedicated GPU pool 'resv-east-prod' at 100% capacity; queue growth detected. autoscaler failing to provision. Trigger: queue_size > 200 for 15m. Impacting reserved tenants with minimal grace pools. Pager sent to oncall.

ana (oncall): Seeing increased error spikes for enterprise tenants — metrics: GPU util 99-100%, queue depth 230->410 over last 10m. Confirming page.

mike (sre): Copy. Pulling autoscaler logs now. Any customer-facing errors?

tilly (acct-mgr): I'm on a call with BrightLeaf (reserved) — they're seeing 503s and long waits, raising urgency. They asked if we have mitigation ETA.

jess (infra): Autoscaler returned repeated API 429 from cloud-provider when trying to request additional instances. Rate-limited. Also some pools show pending instances stuck in PROVISIONING for >8m.

yuki (eng-runtime): Runtime reports many heavy sessions with long seq lengths, KV cache pressure causing GPUs to pin. A few tenants show large pinned KV caches — could be noisy sessions.

ana (oncall): Triage plan: 1) Attempt emergency soft-eviction of idle sessions in resv-east-prod 2) Temporarily open overload route to fallback model variants (lower memory) for reserved tenants 3) Notify customers and open bridge. Anyone object?

mike (sre): +1. I'll run eviction playbook now (runbook: /playbooks/reserved_pool_eviction). Will log commands here.

mike (sre): Running: ```./evictor --pool resv-east-prod --policy soft --age 5m --target 15```

evictor-bot: evictor starting: targeting 15 idle sessions; estimated freed GPUs: 2-4. Progress: 0/15

jess (infra): Spawning manual override to bypass cloud API rate-limits: initiating warm nodes from standby capacity (reserved warm pool) — this will add 2 nodes if successful. Command queued.

paul (eng-platform): Noted that warm pool currently has 1 node; if we use warm pool we risk depletion. Suggest we evict more aggressively from noisy tenants first.

mike (sre): Evictor progress: 7/15 -> 12/15. Freed 3 GPUs so far. Some sessions refused kill due to active transactions (db writes).

ana (oncall): Tilly, can you relay to BrightLeaf we're executing emergency evictions and routing some traffic to lower-memory variants. ETA 10m, may see degraded latency.

tilly (acct-mgr): Messaging sent to primary BrightLeaf contacts, flagged as high. They asked for realtime updates.

incident-bot: Autoscaler attempt failed: provider API 429 -> backoff. Next retry scheduled in 60s.

yuki (eng-runtime): Spawning lighter quantized model variant q4_512 for affected routes. Note: output quality slight regression but reduces memory by ~40%. Rolling config patch to route via q4_512 for tenants with reserved IDs: [BL-123, NOVA-77].

ana (oncall): Good. Start routing change now. Keep one route pinned to original so we can compare errors.

mike (sre): Evictor done: 15 targeted, 13 succeeded. Freed 4 GPUs. Current GPU util 98%. Queue 310.

jess (infra): Warm-pool override succeeded: +2 nodes added but one entered PROVISIONING stuck; forcing restart on healthcheck.

mike (sre): Forced restart completed, node came up. Autoscaler still hitting 429s for additional requests.

yuki (eng-runtime): Routing cutover complete for BL-123 and NOVA-77 to q4_512. Initial telemetry: BL-123 error rate down 40%, tail latency improved but some hallucination/format differences reported.

tilly (acct-mgr): BrightLeaf: preliminary improvement, still seeing occasional 503s on heavy jobs but they're calmer. They'll stay on bridge.

paul (eng-platform): Noticing a single tenant (internal-ml-experiments) consuming multiple long-lived sessions with high sequence lengths — probable noisy neighbor. Who owns that team?

mike (sre): Identifying session owners, pulling job metadata. Session tags: owner=ml-sandbox, created-by=jira/ML-ops.

ana (oncall): If we can locate the owner we should ask them to pause or move to non-reserved pool. If unresponsive, escalate to hard eviction.

mike (sre): Hard eviction prepared: ```./evictor --pool resv-east-prod --policy hard --target owner=ml-sandbox --force``` Will wait 2m for owner contact, then execute. Logging to incident channel after run.

evictor-bot: owner contact not found for sessions matching owner=ml-sandbox.

mike (sre): Executing hard eviction now. Progress: 0/8

mike (sre): Hard eviction done: 8 sessions killed. Freed 6 GPUs. GPU util down to 93%, queue 120.

incident-bot: Autoscaler retry succeeded on attempt #5; new nodes provisioned: 3. Adding capacity.

jess (infra): New nodes joined pool and passed healthchecks. Resv-east-prod capacity increased. Monitoring for churn.

ana (oncall): Summary for incident timeline: - 1710612000: alert triggered - 1710612100: page -> oncall engaged - 1710612200: eviction soft started - 1710612700: forced hard eviction on noisy owner - 1710613000: autoscaler unblocked and scaled +3 nodes - 1710613600: queue reduced, errors substantially reduced.

tilly (acct-mgr): Sent detailed update to BrightLeaf: included mitigation steps and expected follow-up report. They requested postmortem and SLA credit evaluation.

paul (eng-platform): Action items: 1) Investigate cloud provider 429s during scale 2) Add pre-warmed node buffer for reserved pools 3) Improve owner tagging enforcement to avoid noisy tenants in reserved pools 4) Runbook tweak: lower soft-eviction age for reserved pools under pressure.

yuki (eng-runtime): Also propose telemetry change: per-tenant KV cache size alert and automatic throttling policy to prevent single tenant pinning GPUs.

ana (oncall): Agreed. Creating incident ticket and assigning owners. Will schedule a bridge postmortem in next 48h.

mike (sre): Dumping logs and attaching to incident: /incidents/4470001234/artifacts (will upload).

tilly (acct-mgr): I'll coordinate customer postmortem and SLA discussion. Noting BrightLeaf impacted: ~2.5 hours of degraded service window.

ops-triage: Incident closed to paging at 1710615600. Follow-up still open as a Sev2.

ana (oncall): Thanks everyone. If anything flares back up, re-open the thread.

jess (infra): Postmortem owners: paul (cloud 429s), yuki (runtime KV), mike (eviction tuning), ana (customer comms).
